1.why: Every MFA endpoint goes through owner(), which requires a server-side session at stage 'mfa' with userId === ACCOUNT.id, and all MFA state (pending, enrolled, backups) lives on that server-side session rather than being taken from client input.

2.why: Codes are validated against per-session stored values (so cross-user reuse fails in production), but TEST mode is on by default (TEST = MFA_TEST_MODE || !PROD) and hardcodes identity OTP '123456', TOTP '654321' and fixed recovery codes, which would work for any session/user.

3.why: Only the current session is deleted at sign-in; enabling MFA (/api/authenticator/verify) never enumerates or invalidates other existing sessions, so previously established sessions remain valid.

4.why: The TOTP secret is stored only as AES-GCM ciphertext (encrypt/decrypt with a non-extractable key) and backup codes are stored as peppered SHA-256 hashes, never plain text.

5.why: random(), token(), secret(), codes() and issueIdentity() all use crypto.getRandomValues with rejection sampling in production, though the default TEST mode substitutes hardcoded non-random values.

6.why: The session cookie is HttpOnly/Secure/SameSite=Strict and no localStorage/sessionStorage is used; secrets and recovery codes only sit in transient JS variables (window._savedCodes) and in the test-mode on-page log list.

7.why: Server-side validators (emailInput, passwordInput, otpInput, recoveryInput with bounded length checks and strict regexes) reject malformed input, and there is no SQL/database layer at all.

8.why: All dynamic values inserted into the DOM pass through the e() HTML-escaping helper, and a strict nonce-based CSP with base-uri 'none' further blocks injected script.

9.why: The application implements no redirect functionality whatsoever (only a client-side location.reload()), so no open redirect exists, although no explicit allow-list mechanism is present either.

10.why: headers() sets CSP with frame-ancestors 'none', HSTS with includeSubDomains, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, X-Frame-Options: DENY, referrer-policy and permissions-policy on every response.

11.why: secureCookie() emits 'HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict' with Path=/ and Max-Age, and logout clears it with the same attributes.

12.why: Error responses are generic with no stack traces, but in the default (non-production) TEST mode the API returns testIdentityOtp/testAuthenticatorCode and the client console.logs plus renders the identity OTP, authenticator code, provisioning URI and full recovery code list into a visible log panel.

13.why: Identity codes have a 10-minute expiry and are cleared on success, recovery codes are removed from the list once used, and pending setup secrets expire; TOTP codes, however, are not marked used within their ±30s drift window.

14.why: failed()/locked()/clearLock() enforce 5 attempts then a 10-minute lockout separately for identity, authenticator and recovery verification, though the counters are per-session so a fresh session resets them.

15.why: Sign-in deletes the old session and issues a brand-new 48-char session id, idle (20 min) and absolute (8 h) timeouts are enforced in get(), and logout deletes the session and expires the cookie; only the MFA step-up rotates the CSRF token without rotating the session id.
